citation: NIMH. Autism Spectrum Disorder (overview). National Institute of Mental Health, US. Publisher domain: nimh.nih.gov
outcome: Descriptive understanding of autism features and heterogeneity
study_design: Authoritative agency overview (not a primary study)
limitations: General overview, not a primary study; US-centric clinical framing; does not evaluate music-therapy efficacy; emphasizes heterogeneity.
exact_claim_supported: Autism is heterogeneous and support needs vary across individuals and domains (grounds the multidimensional-profile decision and the rejection of a single functioning-level label).

citation: Cochrane. Music therapy for autistic people (systematic review, 2022). Publisher domain: cochranelibrary.com / cochrane.org
population: Autistic people (children and adults, per review scope)
comparison: Varies per review (e.g., no treatment / standard care / active control)
outcome: Social interaction; communication; quality of life; adverse effects (per review scope)
sample_size: Not extracted here; consult the review directly
evidence_certainty: Varies by outcome; low to very low certainty for several outcomes (per the review's certainty ratings) - verify exact ratings before public release
limitations: Evidence certainty varies by outcome; small and heterogeneous underlying studies; the project MUST NOT convert these findings into a clinical-efficacy claim for synthetic outputs.
exact_claim_supported: Music therapy for autistic people has been reviewed systematically, but evidence is uncertain across outcomes; therefore the simulator produces synthetic hypotheses and claims no therapeutic effectiveness.

citation: Cochrane. Auditory integration training and other sound-based interventions for autism spectrum disorder (systematic review). Publisher domain: cochranelibrary.com
sample_size: Not extracted here; consult the review directly
evidence_certainty: Low to very low; insufficient evidence (per the review)
limitations: Distinct evidence base from music therapy; included only to distinguish intervention types; the project does not deliver or evaluate any sound-based intervention.
exact_claim_supported: Sound-based interventions are a separate evidence base from music therapy; the project's music parameters are simulation inputs, not a delivered intervention.

citation: US HHS Office for Human Research Protections. The Belmont Report. Publisher domain: hhs.gov/ohrp
outcome: Ethical principles: Respect for persons; Beneficence; Justice
limitations: US-centric; not specific to autism or AI; principles the project adopts voluntarily.
exact_claim_supported: The project's ethics framing (respect, beneficence, justice, transparency) is grounded in Belmont Report principles.

citation: UNESCO. Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (adopted 2021). Publisher domain: unesco.org
limitations: Broad, non-binding global principles; not autism-specific; informs the project's transparency and accountability posture.
exact_claim_supported: The project's AI-use posture (transparency, accountability, no clinical prediction) is consistent with UNESCO's AI ethics principles.

citation: Autistic Self Advocacy Network (ASAN). Public positions on identity-first language and intervention ethics. Publisher domain: autisticadvocacy.org
limitations: Grey literature / self-advocacy perspective, not peer-reviewed evidence; informs respectful language and participation, not clinical claims.
exact_claim_supported: Use identity-first language ('autistic person'), avoid deficit-only framing and a single functioning-level label (supports the project's language policy).
